sections.html:
Northwest Oklahoma holds Woodward County, seated at the city of Woodward. Its 1,246 square miles are mostly open country, with about 16 people per square mile in 2010. A house on acreage, a farmhouse and a town lot in Woodward, Mooreland or Fort Supply can each raise different tax and access questions, so say which one you own when you call a county office.

The county had 20,470 residents at the 2020 census, and the city of Woodward had 12,133. Agriculture, oil and gas, wind energy and manufacturing all matter locally, and Woodward is the trade center. That mix means demand for houses can swing with the energy cycle.

• Households: 7,728
  • Housing units: 9,386
  • Vacant share of housing units: 17.7%
  • Owner-occupied share of occupied homes: 68.6%
  • Homeowner vacancy rate: 3.3%
  • Rental vacancy rate: 21.0%

Nearly one in five housing units was vacant and the rental vacancy rate was above 21%. Expect a listing to take time here, and weigh that when comparing it with a cash offer. Local population rose and fell with oil, standing at 21,172 in 1980 during a boom and 18,976 by 1990.

Woodward averages about 25.6 inches of precipitation and 17.8 inches of snow a year, and tornadoes are part of its history. An EF3 tornado hit the city on April 14, 2012 and killed six people. On April 9, 1947, a tornado about two miles wide crossed Ellis, Woodward and Woods counties and destroyed about 200 city blocks in Woodward. The National Weather Service ranks it as the deadliest tornado in Oklahoma history.

  • Check whether your roof, windows and siding show hail or wind damage, and keep repair records.
  • Ask your insurer how a storm claim and a sale interact if a claim is still open.
  • Oklahoma's seller disclosure form asks about major fire or tornado damage, so answer it from your records.

The Woodward school district serves more than 2,500 students in an early childhood center, three elementary schools, a middle school and a high school. Other districts reach into the county, including Fort Supply, Sharon-Mutual and Mooreland.

US 412, US 270 and US 183 and State Highways 3, 34 and 15 serve the city, and BNSF's Southern Transcon runs through it. If your house is outside Woodward, have the water source, septic and road access details ready for a buyer, because lenders and inspectors ask about them.

The County Assessor values property and takes exemption applications. The County Treasurer collects the tax. Both offices are at 1600 Main in Woodward.

  • Assessor: Suite 11, phone (580) 256-5061, email assessor@woodwardcounty.org, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Treasurer: Suite 10, phone 580-256-7404, email treasurer@woodwardcounty.org, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday.

The Assessor identifies, classifies and values taxable property for equal taxation. County assessors are overseen by the Oklahoma Tax Commission's Ad Valorem division and audited by the State Auditor and Inspector. Call the Assessor about exemption eligibility, since the office decides each application.

Each year the Assessor posts a fresh calendar, and the pattern repeats. Confirm exact dates with the office.

TimingWhat happens
Early JanuaryAssessment begins, and exemption applications open for the new tax year
Mid-MarchLast day to report personal property and apply for exemptions without penalty
March 31Second half of the prior year's taxes due to the Treasurer
Early AprilDeadline to protest the valuation if no notice was mailed
Mid-AprilMandatory penalty for non-reporting increases
December 31First half of the year's taxes due to the Treasurer

State law puts a ceiling on how fast taxable value can grow. Homestead and agricultural parcels may rise at most 3% a year. Every other kind of real property may rise 5%. Either ceiling lifts when title transfers or improvements are added.

So a new buyer may pay more than you did. To dispute a value, talk to the county assessor first. A mailed increase notice carries its own deadline, so follow that date. With no notice, you have until early April. Still unhappy? Next stops are the Board of Equalization and district court.

Gather support before you file: photos of damage, repair estimates, and a recent independent appraisal if you have one. A lower value helps a seller only while you own the house, but a clean, resolved protest also keeps the file tidy for the title company.

sections.h2: Settling tax and paperwork at closing
sections.html:
Any tax owed gets settled by the title company at the closing table, and the Treasurer's system lists what is due on the parcel. A mistake on the website does not erase an amount owed, so verify figures by phone.

  • Look up the parcel on the Treasurer's website and print the balance.
  • Hand over the Oklahoma disclosure statement or disclaimer ahead of any accepted offer.
  • Make sure the deed and any estate paperwork have been recorded.
  • Book utility, propane or well service changes for closing day.

Get the payoff figure from the Treasurer before fixing a closing date.

sections.h2: What to bring to the county offices
sections.html:
Walking in prepared saves a second trip. Carry a copy of the deed, photo ID and the newest tax statement you have; add recorded estate papers when the house was inherited. At the Assessor you can learn who is listed on the parcel as of January 1, and the Treasurer will print what is owed.

Tell the clerk if you own a town lot, a farmhouse or acreage, since that helps them find the right record. Ask both offices if anything is flagged on the parcel, before a buyer's title search turns it up.

sections.h2: Timeline for a Woodward County sale
sections.html:
Plan the sale in order. First verify the owner of record and the tax balance. Second, collect roof, storm and utility records. Third, choose between listing and a written cash offer. After you accept, a title company searches title, gathers the disclosure statement and schedules closing.

When you sign, any mortgage and unpaid tax are paid out of the proceeds and the remainder is yours. With a tornado or hail claim open, get the insurer's position in writing first.

Our offers cover Woodward County houses in their current condition, with no price promised ahead of time. Paying cash removes the lender, the appraisal and the repair list, a good fit for rural, storm-hit or inherited houses. Put our written number next to a listing plan. Saying no costs you nothing.

faqs.q: When are Woodward County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The second half of the prior year's taxes is due March 31, and the first half of the current year's taxes is due December 31. Confirm exact dates with the Treasurer, 580-256-7404.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Woodward County property tax?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's office is at 1600 Main, Suite 10, in Woodward, open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays. The site also links to an online lookup and payment page.

faqs.q: How do I apply for an exemption in Woodward County?
faqs.a: Applications go to the County Assessor at 1600 Main, Suite 11. File by mid-March each year to avoid a penalty.

faqs.q: Was Woodward hit by a major tornado?
faqs.a: Yes. An EF3 tornado struck the city on April 14, 2012, killing six people, and an F5 tornado on April 9, 1947 destroyed about 200 city blocks.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Woodward County house with an unpaid tax balance?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays what is owed from the proceeds at closing. Get the payoff figure from the Treasurer before you set a closing date.
